resources.string: Double tap with three fingers to toggle full-screen magnification. Works in any app, including games.

A read-only listener on the raw touch input detects a three-finger double tap and toggles full-screen magnification; repeat the gesture to restore. Single taps, long presses, swipes and all system gestures are passed through untouched, so three quick taps can no longer trigger the system zoom by accident. The service needs touch exploration for its gesture channel and magnification to scale the screen. It does not read screen content, has no network access and collects no data.
Find "Triple-Tap Zoom" in Settings, turn it on, and allow touch exploration and magnification.
Tap twice with three fingers to zoom in; repeat to restore. Recognised at the raw input layer, so it works on the home screen, in browsers and inside games.
Center on the three fingers (like iOS)
Some Android 15 builds reset zoom when you switch apps. This switch restores it automatically.

On by default (recommended): every touch is handed to apps and SystemUI from the very first frame. Single taps, long presses, swipes, the bottom home gesture, edge-back and the notification shade all keep their stock behaviour - this app never buffers or intercepts any touch.\n\nOnly turn this off if the three-finger double tap stops responding, to try the legacy takeover mode. That mode briefly buffers touches and on some devices turns a single tap into a phantom long press, so it is not recommended for daily use.
If you enabled the system magnification shortcut before, turn off "Triple-tap to zoom" as well, or it will still fire by accident.

How it works: Shizuku runs a read-only listener on the raw touch input node and recognises a three-finger double tap. Nothing is injected, intercepted or buffered, so single taps, long presses, swipes and every system gesture behave exactly as they do without this app. Magnification is applied by the Android magnification controller; you can still touch normally while zoomed, and drag with two fingers to pan.\n\nNote: after a reboot, start Shizuku once (or run the companion script over USB). This app has no network access, reads no screen content and collects no data.
